The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of four line segments. Then,

${\int }_{-6}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
The graph consists of four parts: the line segment for $x\in [-6,-3],$ the line segment for $x\in (-3,0],$ the line segment for $x\in (0,2],$ and the line segment for $x\in (2,5].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-6}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-6}^{-3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-3}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{4}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-6,-3].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}3(3) \\  & =4.5.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-3,0].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =bh \\  & =3\cdot 1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (0,2].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4+2)(2) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (2,5].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}3(6) \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-6}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}+{A}_{3}+{A}_{4} \\  & =4.5+3+6+9 \\  & =22.5.\end{aligned}
$$
